stories.title: Scientists tested 212 plant-based foods. Every single one contained fungal toxins
summary: A new study has uncovered a surprising concern hiding in popular plant-based foods and drinks.

Researchers tested 212 vegan and vegetarian products sold in the UK, including meat alternatives, oat milk, almond milk, and soy milk, and found that every single one contained at least one potentially harmful fungal toxin.
Known as mycotoxins, these naturally occurring compounds can contaminate grains, legumes, and seeds during farming and storage.

stories.title: This 6-million-year-old whale may have had the most crooked face in mammal history
summary: A bizarre whale that lived roughly 6 million years ago had a face so dramatically crooked that scientists believe it may have been the most asymmetrical of any mammal.

Discovered in Peru, the extinct pygmy sperm whale Scaphokogia huachafo had an enormous downward-curving snout and a skull so distorted that researchers initially thought it had been damaged after death.
Instead, its strange anatomy appears to have been an extraordinary evolutionary adaptation for hunting along the seafloor.

stories.title: Something strange is living beneath the skin of deep-sea pigs
summary: Scientists have discovered a strange bacterium hiding beneath the skin of deep-sea creatures known as sea pigs, revealing an unexpected biological partnership.
The microbe has an unusually tiny genome, yet more than a quarter of its DNA is devoted to making surface proteins, some of them exceptionally large.
Researchers suspect it depends heavily on its host for survival, but what the sea pigs gain in return remains a mystery.

stories.title: Why hydrogen flames can glow orange, then turn nearly invisible
summary: Hydrogen flames can shift from bright orange to nearly invisible depending on something unexpected: tiny amounts of sodium floating in the air.
Scientists say this discovery could help make future hydrogen-powered stoves and ovens safer by replacing visual flame detection with specialized sensors.

stories.title: Developer accused of 'environmental vandalism'
summary: Bellway says the work has been done with an ecologist on site and in compliance with planning consent.

stories.title: Stonehenge’s six-ton mystery deepens as scientists narrow their search
summary: A major new investigation into Stonehenge’s mysterious six-ton Altar Stone has uncovered fresh clues while ruling out several suspected sources.
Once thought to have originated in Wales, the massive sandstone slab is now believed to have come from northeastern Scotland, although researchers have yet to find an exact match.

stories.title: Is free will an illusion? New brain research reveals a surprising twist
summary: New research reveals that the brain makes free choices and forced decisions using surprisingly similar neural processes, with activity building toward a decision before we act.
The discovery challenges assumptions about free will while suggesting that our personal preferences and experiences still shape what we choose.

stories.title: This strange creature lived 309 million years ago, long before the dinosaurs
summary: More than 300 million years ago, long before dinosaurs roamed Earth, the Chicago area was a steamy, swampy landscape teeming with bizarre creatures.
Now, scientists at the Field Museum have identified a previously unrecognized species of ancient amphibian ancestor, revealing new clues about the evolution of frogs and salamanders.

stories.title: Too much exercise could leave your brain stuck in overdrive
summary: Exercising too much without adequate recovery may disrupt brain chemistry in surprising ways.
Scientists found that mice subjected to prolonged, intense training had elevated dopamine levels in a brain region linked to memory and emotions, even 48 hours after exercising.
The discovery could help explain why overtrained athletes sometimes struggle with insomnia, anxiety, and persistent fatigue, although these symptoms were not directly measured.

stories.title: Torrential rain causes widespread flooding in South Florida
summary: Entire neighbourhoods remain under water as disruptions impact schools, roads, hospitals and airports.

stories.title: New discovery reveals what may be holding back room-temperature superconductors
summary: A major breakthrough in superconductivity research has revealed that one of the essential ingredients for electricity to flow without resistance can exist at room temperature.

Scientists discovered that electrons can form stable pairs at much higher temperatures than previously understood, suggesting that a different obstacle may be preventing room-temperature superconductivity.

stories.title: Stormont department failing to protect wild birds, investigation finds
summary: The Office for Environmental Protection said Daera had not complied with environmental law requiring it to classify and update Special Protection Areas.

stories.title: MIT discovers that aging weakens the brain’s nighttime cleaning system
summary: MIT researchers have discovered that the brain’s natural waste-removal system becomes significantly less effective during sleep as people age.
The decline is linked to weaker deep-sleep brain waves and changes in blood flow, potentially offering new clues about why aging increases the risk of Alzheimer's disease and dementia.
Surprisingly, some older adults retain the same powerful cleansing waves seen in younger people.

stories.title: Why do farts smell so bad? The secret is brewing in your gut
summary: The secret behind truly terrible-smelling farts lies in tiny amounts of sulfur-containing gases produced by gut bacteria as they digest food.
Scientists reveal why some foods make farts smell worse, why loud farts aren't always the stinkiest, and how our noses evolved to detect these powerful odors.

stories.title: A little-known protein could be a powerful weapon against Alzheimer’s
summary: Scientists have uncovered a powerful natural defense against Alzheimer’s disease that could open the door to new treatments.

By boosting a protein called SORLA, researchers significantly reduced toxic tau tangles, protected connections between brain cells, and prevented some of the brain shrinkage associated with neurodegeneration in mice.
Removing the protein made the damage worse, highlighting its critical protective role.

stories.title: William and Kate honour Earthshot Prize winners in Mumbai
summary: The Prince and Princess of Wales have said environmental innovators are changing the lives of future generations as they celebrated this year's winners of the Earthshot Prize.

stories.title: I want to know if toxic lagoon fire caused my husband's rare deadly cancer
summary: Steve Williams died of lung cancer 14 years after falling in to a lagoon at a toxic waste dump fire.

stories.title: People asked for views on blue brook pollution
summary: The Environment Agency wants to know how the incident affected visitors, residents and businesses.

stories.title: More than a billion years of Earth's history vanished. Scientists may finally know why
summary: Scientists may have finally explained why up to more than a billion years of Earth's geological history are missing from rocks around the world.

New research suggests that powerful currents deep inside the planet slowly raised and lowered entire continents, allowing erosion to erase vast stretches of geological history before they were buried and preserved.

stories.title: What's gone wrong at Britain's worst bathing site?
summary: The BBC looks at why in a dry summer with few sewage spills, one bathing site failed so many water quality tests.

stories.title: Bizarre deep-sea fish with a see-through head captured in stunning 4K
summary: Deep-sea researchers have captured stunning new footage of an extraordinarily rare fish with a transparent head and rotating eyes nearly 2,000 feet beneath the ocean's surface.
Known as the barreleye fish, this bizarre creature uses its upward-pointing eyes to spot prey before rotating them forward to track its next meal, all while a transparent dome protects them.

stories.title: 125,000 years ago, hippos roamed what is now the vast Arabian Desert
summary: A remarkable 125,000-year-old discovery in Saudi Arabia reveals that early humans once thrived beside enormous lakes filled with wildlife in what is now a vast desert.
Thousands of stone tools and ancient plant remains suggest these prehistoric people used sophisticated hunting techniques, potentially including weapons enhanced with poisonous plant compounds.

stories.title: Autistic brains look surprisingly similar on average. Then scientists looked closer.
summary: Scientists discovered that although people with and without autism show surprisingly similar average brain activity, individuals with autism exhibit much greater differences from one another, especially in regions involved in social understanding.
The findings suggest that traditional research methods may be overlooking crucial differences that could help unlock more personalized autism support.
